Subject: Next steps & evaluation kickoff — Acme evaluation

Hi Alex / Sam,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and really excited about the potential fit between Acme's support automation goals and Redwood's inference runtime. Quick recap from my side:

- Goal: run an internal eval to validate latency, cost, and response quality on your 10k/month support-case generation workload.
- Success criteria (high level): average token latency < 600ms for 1k-token prompts, quality parity with current baseline on the customer-satisfaction prompt set, and cost < $X/token target (we'll finalize numbers in the kickoff).

Attached is a draft evaluation plan that outlines scope, timeline, and deliverables (acme-eval-plan-v1.pdf).

Next step: schedule an evaluation kickoff (trial plan + success criteria + prompt set/evals + roles). Will any of these windows work for you?

- Wed 17 Mar, 11:00 AM PT — 60m (preferred)
- Thu 18 Mar, 9:00 AM PT — 60m
- Fri 19 Mar, 2:00 PM PT — 60m

If you want a technical deep dive during the kickoff, I can bring Connor (solutions engineer) to walk through architecture, data handling, and the eval harness. I can also share a checklist for what we need from your side (sample prompts, a subset of logs, and an authentication token for test reads).

Attachment: acme-eval-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

Thanks — let me know which slot you prefer and who from your team will join.

Best,

Perfect — I'll lock Wed 17 Mar, 11:00 AM PT. Calendar invite coming shortly. Connor will join for the technical deep dive and Neha (customer success) will own the logistics and success criteria capture.

Answers to your questions:
- Network/VPN: for the initial eval we typically run against our hosted endpoints (no VPN required). If you prefer on-prem or VPC later in the eval we can scope that as a follow-up.
- Minimal prompt/sample size: 500–1,000 representative prompts is sufficient for an initial quality sweep. Ideally include a mix of short/long prompts and a few recent failure cases. We'll provide an upload template in the checklist.

Attaching the Redwood trial checklist to make prep easier (redwood-trial-checklist.xlsx). I've also added a short pre-kickoff agenda in the invite: intros, success criteria definition, data/permissions, eval timeline, and immediate next steps.

Action items before kickoff:
- Alex / Acme: share the 500–1,000 prompt samples and indicate which metrics you care about most (latency, relevancy, hallucination rate, etc.).
- Connor / Redwood: prepare architecture slides and the eval harness demo.
- Neha / Redwood: create the shared Drive folder and upload templates + the eval tracker.

Attachment: redwood-trial-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 14KB)

Looking forward to it.

Cheers,

Internal prep notes for the 17 Mar kickoff:

Marissa / Neha,

Thanks for looping me in. I'll prepare the architecture + eval harness demo. A few items I need from Acme (I'll request these in the invite text but can also ask pre-call):

1) Sample prompt set (500–1,000 rows) — CSV preferred, with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior/notes.
2) A small set of representative documents or context snippets if prompts reference internal KB content (redact PII).
3) Confirmation of expected input lengths and any extreme-case prompts (near 1k tokens).

Pre-kickoff checklist for Redwood:
- Build a small eval run on our staging cluster using a 50-prompt smoke test so we can demo results live.
- Prepare slides: infra diagram, auth flow, data handling (retention & logs), and fallback policies.

I'll prep a short slide deck (8–10 slides) and a 10-minute live demo of the eval harness.
